overview: Host Laura Duggan interviewed actor, director, and tour guide Johnny Kinsman about his theater career, Boston Duck Tours, and his historical performance projects. They also discussed historical presentations spotlighting women and Black participants in the American Revolution, as well as Medford historical figure Sarah Bradley Fulton.

items.title: Introduction and Early Career
items.summary: Host Laura Duggan introduced Johnny Kinsman, who discussed his initial introduction to acting through children's theater in Concord, Massachusetts.

items.title: Boston Duck Tours Experience
items.summary: Kinsman described his role as tour quality manager for Boston Duck Tours and the challenge of adapting unscripted historical narration to the pace of city traffic.

items.title: Anthem Theater Company Productions
items.summary: Kinsman shared the founding history of Anthem Theater Company and discussed producing an adaptation of A Christmas Carol and the baseball comedy Romeo versus Juliet.

items.title: Solo Performance of A Christmas Carol
items.summary: Kinsman previewed his upcoming solo performance of A Christmas Carol at the Parker House and Gore Place, which features live musicians and live Foley sound effects.

items.title: Lectures on Revolutionary History and Overlooked Figures
items.summary: Kinsman and Duggan discussed historical lectures highlighting women and Black figures in the American Revolution, including Abigail Adams, Mercy Otis Warren, and local patriot Sarah Bradley Fulton.

items.title: Walking Tours and Sarah Bradley Fulton Memorials
items.summary: After reviewing photos of past events, Kinsman outlined his Concord and Boston walking tours, and Duggan recounted efforts to establish a monument and display historical artifacts connected to Sarah Bradley Fulton in Medford.
